claims.text: The starting material consists of crystalline, near-equiatomic, solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals.
Carbothermal shock synthesis is the proposed single intervention.
Carbothermal shock synthesis can overcome nanoparticle instability during catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
Carbothermal shock can rapidly fabricate high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles within seconds.
Carbothermal shock synthesis can produce metallic nanoparticles while controlling elemental distribution and stoichiometry.
The intervention produces single-phase solid solutions with simple crystal structures.
Configurational disorder can stabilize new oxide phases.
Entropy stabilization of oxide phases enables improved engineering of material properties.
Carbothermal-shock-treated nanoparticles will be more stable than untreated nanoparticles.
Carbothermal-shock-treated nanoparticles will have better catalytic performance than untreated nanoparticles.
The improved catalytic performance can be retained at low noble-metal content.
The proposed application regime is catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
The proposal is bounded to nanoparticles containing five or more metals at equal or near-equal concentrations.
The exact mechanism and property effects of carbothermal shock synthesis are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The initial material and mediator are described as metallic multielement solid solutions, whereas the proposed mechanism invokes stabilization of new oxide phases without specifying oxidation, oxygen incorporation, or how an oxide remains compatible with the claimed metallic solid solution.
